It is India's largest insurance company and its largest [[institutional investor]] with total [[assets under management]] worth {{INRconvert|54.52|lc|lk=on|year=2024}} as of March 2025.{{cite news |last1=Laskar |first1=Anirudh |title=LIC plans makeover of investment strategy |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/lic-plans-makeover-of-investment-strategy-11653068977999.html |access-date=10 February 2023 |work=mint |date=20 May 2022 |language=en}} It is under the ownership of [[Government of India]] and administrative control of the [[Ministry of Finance (India)|Ministry of Finance]].{{cite web |title=Stock Market Today: LIC Beats SBI To Become The Most Valuable PSU |url=https://www.brutimes.com/news/business/stock-market-today-lic-beats-sbi-to-become-the-most-valuable-psu |website=Bru Times News |language=en}} The Life Insurance Corporation of India was established on 1 September 1956, when the [[Parliament of India]] passed the Life Insurance of India Act, nationalising the insurance industry in India. Over 245 insurance companies and provident societies were merged.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mylicindia.com/lic-life-insurance-corporation-of-india/|title=LIC – Life Insurance Corporation Of India|last=Anushka|website=My LIC India|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-18|archive-date=18 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200218071744/https://www.mylicindia.com/lic-life-insurance-corporation-of-india/|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web |title=59th Annual Report |url=http://licindia.in/getattachment/Bottom-Links/annual-report/LIC-Annual-Report-2015-16.pdf.aspx |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826051607/http://licindia.in/getattachment/Bottom-Links/annual-report/LIC-Annual-Report-2015-16.pdf.aspx |archive-date=2016-08-26 |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=licindia.in}} LIC reported 290 million policyholders as of 2019, a total life fund of {{INRconvert|28.3|lc|lk=off|year=2019|mode=historical}}. The company also reported having settled 26 million claims in 2018–19. It ranked 98th on the 2022 [[Fortune Global 500]] list with a revenue of {{INRConvert|775283|c|lk=off|year=2022|mode=historical}} and a profit of {{INRConvert|4415|c|lk=off|year=2022|mode=historical}}.{{Cite web |date=2022-08-04 |title=LIC breaks into Fortune 500 list, Reliance jumps 51 places |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/lic-breaks-into-fortune-500-list-reliance-51-8069514/ |access-date=2022-09-03 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} As of 2026, LIC paid a dividend of Rs. 12,207.25 crore dividend to the centre. The same was presented to the Financial Minister of the Country, Nirmala Sitharaman {{Cite news |date=2026-07-29 |title=LIC pays ₹12,207.25 crore dividend to government |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/lic-pays-1220725-crore-dividend-to-government/article71282502.ece |access-date=2026-08-01 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}. ==History== [[File:LIC Chennai.JPG|thumbnail|[[LIC Building]] at [[Chennai]], was the tallest building in India when it was inaugurated in 1959]] ===Founding organisations=== The Oriental Life Insurance Company, the first company in India to offer life insurance coverage, was established in [[Kolkata]] in 1818 by Bipin Das Gupta. Its primary target market was India.{{cite web|url=http://www.licindia.in/history.htm |title=History |publisher=LIC |access-date=15 December 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216111317/http://www.licindia.in/history.htm |archive-date=16 December 2013 |df=dmy }} [[Surendranath Tagore]] had founded Hindustan Insurance Society around the same time, which later became the Life Insurance Corporation.{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/west-bengal/lunch-on-lotus-leaves/cid/1265929|title=Lunch on lotus leaves|website=www.telegraphindia.com|access-date=19 December 2018}} The Bombay Mutual Life Assurance Society was formed in 1870, almost half a century later. It was the first native insurance provider of Western India. Other insurance companies established in the pre-independence era include: * Postal Life Insurance (PLI) was introduced on 1 February 1884 * Bharat Insurance Company (1896) * [[United India Insurance Company|United India]] (1906) * National Indian (1906) * [[National Insurance Company|National Insurance]] (1906) * Co-operative Assurance (1906) * Hindustan Co-operatives (1907) * The New India Assurance Co Ltd (1919) * Indian Mercantile * General Assurance * Swadeshi Life (later Bombay Life) * Sahyadri Insurance (Merged into LIC, 1986) These companies were established when India was marked mostly by turbulent economic and political conditions including the [[Indian rebellion of 1857]], [[World War I]] and [[World War II]]. The effect of these events led to a high liquidation rate of life insurance companies in India and adversely affected the faith of the public in the value of obtaining life insurance. ===Nationalisation in 1956=== In January 1956, LIC was nationalised in two stages: initially, the company's management was taken over by the government by an ordinance in January{{Cite web |title=LIC History - Decades of Trust, Excellence, and Financial Security |url=https://licindia.in/history |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=Liferay DXP |language=en-US}}, and then the [[Parliament of India]] enacted the [https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1632/1/A195631.pdf Life Insurance Corporation of India Act, 1956]. In 1960, a foreign branch was established in the [[United Kingdom]] {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. The corporation obtained a certification of registration from the IRDAI to undertake life insurance business, and was renewed under article 3A of the Insurance Act {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. === Post-Nationalisation Measures === In 1981, the corporation implemented a reorganisation policy to give effect to operations decentralisation and proper decision making. Jana Raksha Policy was formulated to cater to the rural masses {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. Installation of microprocessors was first initiated in October by the corporation and the recruitment under sports quota started. In 1987, the corporation introduced a group insurance called- LAGLI (Landless Agricultural Labourers Group Insurance) {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. During this year, LICs prestigious Jeevan Bharati Building was inaugurated by the union minister [[N. D. Tiwari|N.D Tiwari]]. In 1989, an associate recognised LIC Housing Finance Limited was set up by the corporation {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. The Corporation established a mutual funds as a trust on 20th April, 1989. The RGLIS (Rural Group Life Insurance Scheme) was launched on 15th August, 1995 {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. On 1998, the first IVRS was inaugurated in [[Mumbai]]. Moreover, 150 touch screen based information kiosks were set up across the country, enabling customers to get information on policies, new plans and bonuses {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. In 1999, LIC (International) EC extended its operations to [[Qatar]]. In 2000, they extended their operations to [[Nepal]] through a subsidiary, Life Insurance Corporation {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. In 2001, the first unit linked insurance plan, BIMA Plus was launched. LIC signed its first strategic alliance with Corporation bank that year as well {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. ===Initial public offering=== [[Finance minister of india|Finance Minister]] [[Nirmala Sitharaman]] announced a proposal for an [[initial public offering]] (IPO) for the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) in the [[2021 Union budget of India]].{{cite web |date=10 February 2021 |title=LIC IPO: Good news for LIC insurance policy holders! Modi government confirms this big development |url=https://www.zeebiz.com/market-news/news-lic-ipo-good-news-for-lic-insurance-policy-holders-modi-government-confirms-this-big-development-149083 |access-date=7 March 2021 |website=Zee Business}} In 2021, the Indian government also proposed to enhance LIC's authorised capital to {{INRConvert|25000|c|lk=off|year=2021|mode=historical}} to facilitate its public listing.{{cite news |date=8 March 2021 |title=India: Govt plans to increase authorized capital of LIC by 2.5x to prepare for IPO |url=https://www.asiainsurancereview.com/News/View-NewsLetter-Article/id/75834/Type/eDaily/India-Govt-plans-to-increase-authorised-capital-of-LIC-by-2-5x-to-prepare-for-IPO |access-date=22 April 2021 |publisher=Asia Insurance Review}}{{cite news |title=Government proposes to hike LIC authorised capital to Rs 25,000 crore |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/ipos/fpos/government-proposes-to-hike-lic-authorised-capital-to-rs-25000-crore/articleshow/81375724.cms |access-date=7 March 2021 |website=The Economic Times}} The LIC IPO opened to the public on 4 May 2022, and concluded on 9 May 2022. The Government of India aimed to raise ₹21,000 crore through the IPO, which was significantly lower than the initially expected ₹65,000 to ₹70,000 crore by diluting a 5% equity stake.{{Cite web |date=12 April 2022 |title=LIC IPO size cut by one-third, valuation by half |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/investing/lic-ipo-size-cut-by-one-third-valuation-by-half/107911 |access-date=2022-04-26 |website=www.fortuneindia.com |language=en}} Instead, the IPO offered a 3.5% stake, valuing the company at approximately ₹6 lakh crore.{{cite news |last=Kar |first=Sharmita |date=4 May 2022 |title=LIC IPO: India's biggest IPO has opened - Here are 10 things you should know |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business/lic-ipo-india-s-biggest-ipo-opens-tomorrow-here-are-10-things-you-should-know-101651562549844.html |work=Hindustan Times |access-date=1 September 2024}}{{cite news |last=Ranjan |first=Abhinav |date=10 May 2022 |title=LIC IPO closes: Allotment on May 12, check grey market premium |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/business/markets/lic-ipo-allotment-subscription-status-link-date-may-12-lic-share-price-listing-date-gmp-grey-market-premium-2022-05-10-775393 |work=India TV |access-date=1 September 2024}} The company's market value increased by $30 billion over two years after listing.{{cite news |last=Sinha |first=Vaishnawi |date=30 January 2024 |title=LIC shares touch record high two years after IPO, market value spikes by $30 billion |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business/lic-shares-touch-record-high-two-years-after-ipo-market-value-spikes-by-30-billion-101706625712379.html |work=Hindustan Times |access-date=1 September 2024}} As of December 2024, LIC's listed holdings were valued at approximately $177 billion. By February 18, 2025, they declined to $166.5 billion, reflecting a 5.7% mark-to-market loss of $10.1 billion.{{Cite web |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/lic-suffers-rs-84-000-crore-dent-in-portfolio-amid-stock-market-crash-125021900240_1.html |title=LIC suffers Rs 84,000 crore dent in portfolio amid stock market crash |first=Business |last=Standard |website=www.business-standard.com}} In May 2026, LIC shareholders approved a 1:1 bonus share issue, under which eligible shareholders would receive one additional share for every existing share held. It is the first bonus issue announced by the company after listing.{{Cite web |title=1:1 Bonus Issue: First-ever bonus for 69-year-old insurance giant LIC as shareholders approve share issue; check details |url=https://www.zeebiz.com/market-news/news-11-bonus-issue-first-ever-bonus-for-69-year-old-insurance-giant-lic-as-shareholders-approve-share-issue-check-details-395849 |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=Zee Business |language=en}} In January 2026, Citi recommended LIC shares with a target price of ₹1,345, implying a potential upside of 66.16% from the prevailing market price.[https://www.etnownews.com/markets/lic-stock-trades-14-below-ipo-price-analysts-see-66-upside-from-current-levels-article-153476803 In January 2026, Citi recommended LIC shares with a target price of Rs 1,345, implying a potential upside of 66.16% from the prevailing market price.] ==Structure== The Central Office of LIC is based out of [[Mumbai]]. There are a total of 8 zonal offices, located in [[Delhi]], [[Chennai]], [[Mumbai]], [[Hyderabad]], [[Kanpur]], [[Kolkata]], [[Bhopal]] and [[Patna]]. ===Liberalisation post 2000s=== In August 2000, the [[Indian Government]] embarked on a program to liberalise the insurance sector and opened it up to the private sector. The LIC benefited from this process and in 2013 reported that the first year premium [[compound annual growth rate]] (CAGR) was 24.53% while total life premium CAGR was 19.28%, matching the growth of the life insurance industry and outperforming general economic growth.{{cite web|author=CA. Nirmal Ghorawat |url=http://canirmalg.wordpress.com/2013/01/31/few-perspectives-on-life-insurance-in-india/ |title=Perspectives on Life Insurance Industry in India « CA. Nirmal Ghorawat's Blog |publisher=Canirmalg.wordpress.com |date=31 January 2013 |access-date=14 June 2013}} === Employees === A scheme of incentive bonus to development officers came into existence. In 1980, the corporation began to recruit development officers and the NIA sponsored jointly with GIC and its subsidiaries were founded {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. ==Golden Jubilee Foundation== The LIC Golden Jubilee Foundation was established in 2006 as a charity organisation. The entity has the aim of promoting education, alleviating poverty, and providing better living conditions for the underprivileged. The Golden Jubilee Scholarship award is one of the best known parts of the foundation. Each year, this award is given to the meritorious students in the 12th standard who wish to continue their studies, and have a parental income less than {{INRConvert|2|l|lk=l}}.{{cite web|url=https://www.kcgmckarnal.org/lic-scholarship/|title=LIC Scholarship|date=22 December 2021|access-date=26 December 2021|archive-date=25 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230125162219/https://www.kcgmckarnal.org/lic-scholarship/|url-status=dead}} ==Holdings== The LIC invests in sectors such as banks, cement, chemicals and fertilisers, electricity and transmission, electrical and electronics, engineering, construction and infrastructure, fast-moving consumer goods, finance and investments, healthcare, hotels, information technology, metals and mining, motor vehicles, and ancillaries, oil and natural resources, retail, textiles, transportation, and logistics.{{Cite news |title=Union government, LIC to divest over 60 per cent stake in IDBI Bank |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/union-government-lic-to-divest-over-60-per-cent-stake-in-idbi-bank/articleshow/94706287.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2022-11-10}} == Other Information == * Yogakshema, an architectural landmark, is the corporate office of LIC, and was inaugurated by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru. * In 1970, a commemorative stamp and postcard was issues through Indian post offices and telegraphs, depicting the legacy of the firm {{Cite web |title=Life Insurance Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/life-insurance-corporation-of-india/summary |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}. ==See also== * [[Insurance in India]] * [[Insurance]] * [[LIC Housing Finance]] ==References== {{reflist|2}} == External links == {{commons category|Life Insurance Corporation of India}} * {{Official website}} {{Insurance in India}} {{Indian PSU}} {{Major insurance companies}}{{Financial services in India}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Life Insurance Corporation Of India}} [[Category:2022 initial public offerings]] [[Category:Financial services companies based in Mumbai]] [[Category:Government-owned insurance companies of India]] [[Category:Financial services companies established in 1956]] [[Category:Life insurance companies of India]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1956]] [[Category:Life Insurance Corporation| ]] [[Category:Mutual funds of India]] [[Category:Exchange-traded funds]] [[Category:Investment management companies of India]] [[Category:1956 establishments in Bombay State]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]

Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) is an Indian public sector life insurance company headquartered in Mumbai. It is India's largest insurance company and its largest institutional investor with total assets under management worth ₹54.52 lakh crore (US$570 billion) as of March 2025. It is under the ownership of Government of India and administrative control of the Ministry of Finance.
The Life Insurance Corporation of India was established on 1 September 1956, when the Parliament of India passed the Life Insurance of India Act, nationalising the insurance industry in India. Over 245 insurance companies and provident societies were merged.
LIC reported 290 million policyholders as of 2019, a total life fund of ₹28.3 lakh crore (US$401.87 billion). The company also reported having settled 26 million claims in 2018–19. It ranked 98th on the 2022 Fortune Global 500 list with a revenue of ₹775,283 crore (US$98.63 billion) and a profit of ₹4,415 crore (US$561.67 million).
As of 2026, LIC paid a dividend of Rs. 12,207.25 crore dividend to the centre. The same was presented to the Financial Minister of the Country, Nirmala Sitharaman .
